```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

source("R/setup.R")
```

```{r}
#| label: load
#| include: false

de <- readRDS("data/de_results.rds")
logcpm <- readRDS("data/logcpm.rds")
y2 <- readRDS("data/y2.rds")
samples <- y2$samples %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("sample") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(group = factor(group, levels = group_levels))

res <- de$HDM_in_WT
```

## Overview

Pathway analysis places the wild-type HDM response in the context of curated KEGG pathways [@kanehisa2000kegg]. Two complementary approaches are used [@wu2021clusterprofiler]:

- **Over-representation analysis (ORA)** asks whether strongly changed genes (FDR < 0.05 and at least two-fold) fall in a pathway more often than chance. Up- and downregulated genes are tested separately, so that a pathway's direction is clear.
- **Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA)** uses every tested gene, ranked by signed significance, and asks whether a pathway's genes cluster at the top or bottom of the ranking [@subramanian2005gsea]. It needs no cut-off and picks up coordinated modest shifts.

In both, the background is the set of genes that passed expression filtering, not the whole genome. Using the whole genome would inflate enrichment for any lung-expressed pathway.

```{r}
#| label: kegg-inputs

res_kegg <- res %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(ENTREZID)) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(ENTREZID, .keep_all = TRUE)

universe_ids <- res_kegg$ENTREZID
up_ids   <- res_kegg %>% dplyr::filter(FDR < fdr_cutoff, logFC >=  lfc_cutoff) %>% dplyr::pull(ENTREZID)
down_ids <- res_kegg %>% dplyr::filter(FDR < fdr_cutoff, logFC <= -lfc_cutoff) %>% dplyr::pull(ENTREZID)

# Signed -log10(P) ranks genes by evidence and direction together, which is
# more stable than ranking by fold change alone for lowly expressed genes.
rank_stat <- with(res_kegg, sign(logFC) * -log10(PValue))
gene_list <- sort(setNames(rank_stat, res_kegg$ENTREZID), decreasing = TRUE)
```

The ORA input is `r length(up_ids)` upregulated and `r length(down_ids)` downregulated genes, against a background of `r comma(length(universe_ids))` genes with an Entrez ID.

## Over-representation analysis

```{r}
#| label: kegg-ora

ora <- clusterProfiler::compareCluster(
  geneClusters  = list(Up = up_ids, Down = down_ids),
  fun           = "enrichKEGG",
  organism      = "mmu",
  universe      = universe_ids,
  pvalueCutoff  = 0.05,
  pAdjustMethod = "BH"
)
ora <- clusterProfiler::setReadable(ora, OrgDb = org.Mm.eg.db, keyType = "ENTREZID")

# Strip the species suffix KEGG appends to every pathway name
ora@compareClusterResult$Description <- sub(" - Mus musculus.*$", "", ora@compareClusterResult$Description)

ora_tbl <- as.data.frame(ora) %>% dplyr::filter(p.adjust < 0.05)
readr::write_csv(ora_tbl, "tables/kegg_ora_HDM_in_WT.csv")
```

`r sum(ora_tbl$Cluster == "Up")` KEGG pathways are enriched among HDM-induced genes and `r sum(ora_tbl$Cluster == "Down")` among HDM-repressed genes (adjusted P < 0.05).

```{r}
#| label: fig-kegg-ora
#| fig-cap: "KEGG pathways over-represented among genes up- or downregulated by HDM in WT lung (top 15 per direction). Dot size is the fraction of input genes in the pathway; colour is the adjusted P value."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 9

p_ora <- enrichplot::dotplot(ora, showCategory = 15, label_format = 45) +
  labs(x = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9))

save_plot(p_ora, "kegg_ora_dotplot.png", width = 9, height = 9)
p_ora
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-kegg-ora
#| tbl-cap: "Top enriched KEGG pathways per direction, with the leading genes from the input list."

ora_tbl %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Cluster) %>%
  dplyr::slice_min(p.adjust, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    Direction = Cluster, Pathway = Description, Genes = GeneRatio,
    `Adj. P` = signif(p.adjust, 2),
    `Example genes` = purrr::map_chr(strsplit(geneID, "/"), ~ paste(head(.x, 8), collapse = ", "))
  ) %>%
  nice_table()
```

HDM-induced genes fall into three groups of pathways. The KEGG *Asthma*, *IL-17 signalling* and *Chemokine signalling* pathways are also enriched, though they rank lower because they are small or overlap with the larger terms.

- **Leukocyte recruitment.** Cytokine–cytokine receptor interaction and viral protein interaction with cytokines are driven by the chemokines *Ccl6*, *Ccl8*, *Ccl9*, *Ccl11* (eotaxin), *Ccl20* and *Cxcl3* and their receptors *Ccr1*, *Ccr3* and *Ccr5*, together with *Il21* and *Csf2* (GM-CSF).
- **Complement and innate effector functions.** Complement and coagulation cascades, neutrophil extracellular trap formation and *Staphylococcus aureus* infection all rest on *C3*, *C3ar1*, *C1q* genes, Fc-γ receptors and *Itgb2*.
- **Cell proliferation.** Homologous recombination and the histone-rich pathways (*Systemic lupus erythematosus*, *Alcoholism*) pick up replication genes (*Rad51*, *Chek1*, *Cdk1*) and replication-dependent histones, a sign of the immune cells proliferating in the inflamed lung.

The repressed set is smaller. It points to xenobiotic and glutathione metabolism (*Gstm1*, *Gsta3*, *Cyp2f2*, the cytochrome P450 enzymes of club cells), neuroactive ligand–receptor genes, and a *Malaria* term carried by haemoglobin genes, which reflects slightly less blood in HDM lungs (see the [QC chapter](QC.qmd#tissue-contamination)).

### Gene–pathway network

A network view shows how the leading induced pathways share genes. Pathways that look distinct by name often rest on the same core of cytokines and receptors.

```{r}
#| label: fig-kegg-cnet
#| fig-cap: "Gene–concept network for the six most enriched KEGG pathways among HDM-induced genes. Gene nodes are coloured by log2 fold change."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8

ora_up <- clusterProfiler::enrichKEGG(up_ids, organism = "mmu", universe = universe_ids,
                                      pvalueCutoff = 0.05)
ora_up <- clusterProfiler::setReadable(ora_up, OrgDb = org.Mm.eg.db, keyType = "ENTREZID")
ora_up@result$Description <- sub(" - Mus musculus.*$", "", ora_up@result$Description)

fc_vec <- setNames(res$logFC, res$SYMBOL)

p_cnet <- enrichplot::cnetplot(ora_up, showCategory = 6, color.params = list(foldChange = fc_vec),
                               cex.params = list(gene_label = 0.6, category_label = 0.8)) +
  scale_colour_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "grey90", high = "#B2182B", name = "log2FC")

save_plot(p_cnet, "kegg_ora_cnetplot.png", width = 10, height = 8)
p_cnet
```

## Gene set enrichment analysis

```{r}
#| label: kegg-gsea

gsea <- clusterProfiler::gseKEGG(
  geneList      = gene_list,
  organism      = "mmu",
  minGSSize     = 15,
  maxGSSize     = 500,
  pvalueCutoff  = 0.05,
  pAdjustMethod = "BH",
  seed          = TRUE,
  eps           = 0
)
gsea <- clusterProfiler::setReadable(gsea, OrgDb = org.Mm.eg.db, keyType = "ENTREZID")
gsea@result$Description <- sub(" - Mus musculus.*$", "", gsea@result$Description)

gsea_tbl <- as.data.frame(gsea)
readr::write_csv(gsea_tbl, "tables/kegg_gsea_HDM_in_WT.csv")
```

GSEA finds `r sum(gsea_tbl$NES > 0)` pathways shifted towards induction and `r sum(gsea_tbl$NES < 0)` towards repression (adjusted P < 0.05).

```{r}
#| label: fig-kegg-gsea
#| fig-cap: "Top KEGG pathways from GSEA, split by direction (activated = enriched among HDM-induced genes). Dot size is the number of core-enrichment genes; x-axis is the gene ratio."
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 8

p_gsea <- enrichplot::dotplot(gsea, showCategory = 12, split = ".sign", label_format = 45) +
  facet_grid(. ~ .sign) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9))

save_plot(p_gsea, "kegg_gsea_dotplot.png", width = 11, height = 8)
p_gsea
```

### Running enrichment scores

Running-score plots show where a pathway's genes fall along the ranked list. A sharp early peak means the pathway's genes sit among the most strongly induced genes. The three plotted pathways are the top-ranked activated pathway, the asthma pathway and the top-ranked suppressed pathway.

```{r}
#| label: fig-kegg-running
#| fig-cap: "GSEA running enrichment scores for selected KEGG pathways. Ticks mark pathway genes along the ranked list (left = most HDM-induced)."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7

top_up_id   <- gsea_tbl %>% dplyr::filter(NES > 0) %>% dplyr::slice_min(p.adjust, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% dplyr::pull(ID)
top_down_id <- gsea_tbl %>% dplyr::filter(NES < 0) %>% dplyr::slice_min(p.adjust, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% dplyr::pull(ID)
asthma_id   <- intersect("mmu05310", gsea_tbl$ID)

show_ids <- unique(c(top_up_id, asthma_id, top_down_id))

p_run <- enrichplot::gseaplot2(gsea, geneSetID = show_ids,
                               title = NULL, base_size = 10,
                               color = c("#D55E00", "#CC79A7", "#0072B2")[seq_along(show_ids)])

draw_run <- function() print(p_run)
save_grid(draw_run, "kegg_gsea_running_score.png", width = 10, height = 7)
p_run
```

### Ridge plot

The ridge plot shows the distribution of the ranking statistic for core-enrichment genes in each pathway. It gives a feel for how strong and how uniform each pathway's shift is.

```{r}
#| label: fig-kegg-ridge
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of signed −log10 P for core-enrichment genes in the top 20 GSEA pathways."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 9

p_ridge <- enrichplot::ridgeplot(gsea, showCategory = 20, label_format = 45) +
  labs(x = "Signed −log10 P (core enrichment genes)") +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9))

save_plot(p_ridge, "kegg_gsea_ridgeplot.png", width = 9, height = 9)
p_ridge
```

## From pathways to mechanisms

Many enriched KEGG pathways overlap heavily, and the infection-named pathways (for example *Leishmaniasis* or *Staphylococcus aureus infection*) enter only because they share cytokine, complement and MHC genes. To make the result easier to read, enriched pathways are grouped into broader biological themes with simple keyword rules (see `R/gene_panels.R`). Each induced gene is then assigned to the theme of its most significant pathway.

```{r}
#| label: mechanism-table

mech <- ora_up@result %>%
  dplyr::filter(p.adjust < 0.05) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(theme = assign_kegg_theme(Description)) %>%
  dplyr::select(Description, theme, p.adjust, geneID) %>%
  tidyr::separate_rows(geneID, sep = "/") %>%
  dplyr::rename(SYMBOL = geneID) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(p.adjust) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(SYMBOL, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(res %>% dplyr::select(SYMBOL, logFC, FDR), by = "SYMBOL")

readr::write_csv(mech, "tables/genes_by_mechanism.csv")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-mechanism
#| tbl-cap: "HDM-induced genes grouped into mechanism themes via their most significant KEGG pathway."

mech %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Theme = theme) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    Pathways = dplyr::n_distinct(Description),
    Genes = dplyr::n(),
    `Top genes by fold change` = paste(SYMBOL[order(-logFC)][1:min(8, dplyr::n())], collapse = ", "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(Genes)) %>%
  nice_table()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-mechanism-heatmap
#| fig-cap: "Expression of HDM-induced genes grouped by mechanism theme (top 12 genes per theme by fold change). Values are row z-scores of logCPM across all four groups."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 12

mech_plot <- mech %>%
  dplyr::group_by(theme) %>%
  dplyr::slice_max(logFC, n = 12, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(theme = factor(theme, levels = names(sort(table(mech$theme), decreasing = TRUE)))) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(theme, dplyr::desc(logFC)) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(SYMBOL, block = as.character(theme))

ht_mech <- grouped_zscore_heatmap(logcpm, mech_plot, samples, row_fontsize = 7)
draw_mech <- function() ComplexHeatmap::draw(ht_mech, merge_legends = TRUE)
save_grid(draw_mech, "heatmap_mechanisms.png", width = 8, height = 12)
draw_mech()
```
